claims.claim: Reachability is exactly a sparse unary congruence-closure query.
claims.evidence: Let θ be the least equivalence such that two same-box edges (o,X,t),(o',X,t') with t θ t' force o θ o'. Induction over the construction of θ realizes equality, reversal, concatenation, and each fold as protected-stack paths: push X along the first edge, follow the previously realized neutral path between targets above XS, then pop along the reverse second edge. Conversely, every path that does not pop its protected suffix has a well-nested word; induction on its concatenation/outermost-matched-pair decomposition places its endpoints in θ. Before the terminal done transition, the bottom symbol is protected, so the maze exits exactly when the start is θ-equivalent to an outer-pin wire. Writing each edge as the sparse equation f_X(t)=o gives precisely a partial-unary congruence instance. Exhaustive checks on all 512 one-box graphs over three wires agreed with protected-stack configuration reachability.
claims.search_method: Direct two-inclusion proof using protected Dyck-path decomposition and closure-derivation realization, supplemented by exhaustive finite-model comparison.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic O(B+(W+E) log(W+E))-time, O(W+E+B)-space algorithm, eliminating the dense W·B initialization.
claims.evidence: The sparse-map invariant is sufficient. Every queued origin equality is forced because its two retained edges have the same box and targets already in one component. Hence every performed merge lies in θ. When the queue empties, each target component has at most one retained edge per box; deleted representatives have had their origins equated with a surviving representative, so the resulting partition is stable for every original edge. Leastness then gives the reverse inclusion and equality with θ. A collision deletes one representative, so there are at most E collision records; there are at most W−1 successful component merges. Smaller-to-larger member relabeling costs O(W log W). Deterministic split/join balanced-tree union costs O(m log(n/m+1)) for map sizes m≤n; charging deleted entries once and surviving entries to map growth gives O(E log(E+1)) total. Initial bounded-key radix construction costs O(W+E+B), and maps, members, retained edges, and queued records use O(W+E+B) space. The checker matched collision-driven and literal closure on all 262,144 two-box edge subsets over three wires and confirmed collisions never exceeded E.
claims.search_method: Invariant, least-fixed-point, deletion-count, smaller-to-larger, and deterministic meld-cost analysis, plus exhaustive comparison with literal closure.

claims.claim: Both outcomes have certificates of size O(W+E) verifiable deterministically in O(W+E+B) time.
claims.evidence: For a negative instance, bounded wire labels define an equivalence P. Sorting edges by (X,P(t)) and requiring one P(o) value per group verifies stability in O(W+E+B). Since θ is contained in every stable equivalence, separation in P implies separation in θ; θ itself proves completeness. For a positive instance, leaves certify reflexivity and each chronological internal forest node combines two earlier disjoint components using same-box edges whose targets lie below an earlier certified node q. Induction proves every node's leaves θ-equivalent. Chronological references and unique parents form a forest; one DFS supplies subtree intervals for constant-time membership checks. Any successful closure merge sequence yields at most W−1 internal nodes, and a root containing the start and an outer-pin wire proves exit. Thus size is linear in words and verification is O(W+E+B). Across all 512 one-box three-wire graphs, the checker validated generated forests for 4,608 ordered pairs and checked 861 stable partitions against the least closure.
claims.search_method: Separate soundness/completeness proofs for stable coarsening certificates and chronological fold forests, with exhaustive small-instance validation.

claims.claim: The target O(W+E+B) bound holds for graded dual graphs: graphs admitting an integer rank ρ with ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 for every edge (o,X,t).
claims.evidence: Induction on folding shows θ relates only equal-rank wires. Consequently, all rank-r merges depend exclusively on already-final rank-(r−1) target classes. Grouping rank-r edges by (X,class(t)), adding a star between each group's origins, and taking ordinary connected components therefore computes exactly the final rank-r classes without iteration at that rank. Sparse timestamp lists implement pair grouping with O(B+W) initialized storage and O(1) work per occurrence; all stars contain O(E) edges. Rank existence is checked by propagating the exact constraints ρ(o)−ρ(t)=1 through each weak component. A consistent component may be shifted so its minimum is zero, and its rank span is at most W−1, allowing linear bucket ordering. The checker matched layered and literal closure on all 65,536 admissible two-box subsets for ranks (0,0,1,1,2,2), and rank recognition matched exhaustive integer assignments on all 512 directed three-wire graphs.
claims.search_method: Rank-preservation induction, dependency-layer decomposition, sparse grouping analysis, and exhaustive graded-instance and potential-consistency checks.

claims.claim: Repeated global fixed-point rescanning can require Θ(W) changing rounds even with one box and E=Θ(W).
claims.evidence: For wires z,a_0,b_0,…,a_n,b_n, the two edges into z merge only a_0,b_0 in the first synchronous round. Inductively, after round k exactly the pairs a_j,b_j for j<k have merged, so the edges targeting a_{k−1},b_{k−1} first merge a_k,b_k in round k+1. No rule merges z or distinct levels. Thus there are n+1 changing rounds with W=2n+3 and E=2n+2. Distinct pins realize all edges with the single box X. Conversely, every changing round strictly reduces the number of equivalence classes, giving at most W−1 changing rounds. The exact simulation confirmed every formula and round invariant for n=0 through 128.
claims.search_method: Explicit one-box family, induction on synchronous rounds, class-count upper bound, and exact simulation of 129 instances.

claims.claim: The bounded-key radix sorts used above rely only on the standard lexicographic stable-pass invariant, not on preservation of earlier-key blocks.
claims.evidence: Stable sorting records (a,b) first by b and then by a orders distinct a values in the final pass, while stability preserves nondecreasing b order only within each equal-a group. This is exactly lexicographic (a,b) order and requires no preservation of global b-blocks; such blocks can be rearranged by the a pass. Therefore (t,X) correctly uses passes X then t, and (X,P(t)) uses passes P(t) then X. Their key ranges are bounded by B and W, so counting passes take O(W+E+B) time and space. The checker compared the two-pass result with lexicographic sorting on all 66,430 sequences of length at most five over {0,1,2}² and explicitly confirmed disruption of the earlier-key order.
claims.search_method: Formal stable-sort invariant proof and exhaustive enumeration of bounded pair-key sequences.
